Hi Jordan,

Thanks again for the conversation last week. SignalPeak is ready to run a small proof-of-concept to route our tracing and logs through an OTLP relay into Datadog so we can correlate application traces with model inference telemetry. We want to validate:

- end-to-end trace continuity (app -> OTLP -> Redwood -> Datadog APM)
- sampling/volume controls to avoid token cost spikes
- prefix/KV caching behavior for repeated inference paths

Target: 2-week pilot with a single microservice and a small user cohort (approx 5k requests/day). We can provide sanitized sample traces and an S3 link to logs.

Are you able to run an initial discovery call this week to scope the integration and confirm data handling? Also: any standard SOW/template you prefer for pilot engagements?

Thanks,

Thanks Jordan / Maya — looping in a few technical notes ahead of discovery so we have concrete items for the call: 

- Preferred flow: app -> OTLP collector (SignalPeak) -> Redwood OTLP relay -> Redwood runtime -> Datadog APM (via OTLP or native Datadog exporter). We’ll validate both OTLP->OTLP and OTLP->Datadog-export paths.
- Data volume: if you expect ~5k inference requests/day with average 1.2k tokens per request, we need to test sampling at the request-level and token-level estimates. Please share a 48-72h sample.
- Auth: we support API-key + mTLS for private relays; for hosted pilot, token-based relay is easiest. Let us know if you require keys in a KMS.
- Retention & PII: send sanitized payloads; we’ll provide a redaction checklist.

I attached a short tech note with the pilot checklist and required sample formats.

Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
